title: Observing with simple equipment
keyIdea: Scientists look closely. A hand lens makes small things look bigger, so you can see details that were there all along. Move it until the view is sharp, then describe what you see with looking words: colour, shape, size, texture and pattern. Use your observations to compare and identify things, and pick the right tool for each question.
familyTip: Take a hand lens outside and look at a leaf, some bark or a stone together. Ask for three looking words each, like bumpy, grey or stripy. Then find two leaves that look the same and look closely for one difference. Remind your child never to look at the Sun through the lens.

visual.caption: Which tool answers each question? Drag each card into a box, or tap the card then a box.

items: See the tiny hairs on a leaf
How long does the ice take to melt?
Count the legs on an ant

lab.caption: Flagship lab: drag a hand lens over a leaf to find tiny things, make it sharp, describe a shell, compare two leaves, match tools and stay safe.

kid: A hand lens is a round glass you hold. It makes small things look bigger. You can see tiny bits you could not see before. The tiny bits were there all the time. The lens does not make them grow. It just helps your eyes.
If it looks blurry, move the lens a bit. Go closer or farther until it looks sharp.
Say what you see. Use words for colour, shape, size and feel. Say bumpy, round or stripy. Nice and good do not tell what you see.
Look at two things side by side to find what is the same and what is not. Use a ruler to find how long. Use a timer to see how much time. Never look at the Sun with a lens.
adult: Ages 5 to 7. National Curriculum in England, Key Stage 1 working scientifically: observing closely, using simple equipment, and identifying and classifying. Children use observations to describe, compare and group things.

A hand lens is a convex lens. Held close to the eye, with the object brought in until the image is sharp, it gives an enlarged view, typically 2 to 10 times. The object is unchanged: the lens reveals detail already present. If the object is too close or too far from the lens, the image blurs. Good observation uses specific vocabulary for observable properties (colour, shape, size, texture, pattern) and records similarities and differences when two objects are compared side by side. Choosing equipment means matching it to the question: a hand lens for fine detail, a ruler for length, a timer for time.

Common mistakes: thinking the lens makes the object itself bigger; pressing the lens flat on the object or giving up when the view is blurry; describing with opinion words such as nice or pretty; calling two things the same after a glance; mixing up how long (length) with how long (time); and looking at the Sun through a lens, which can damage eyes.

In the lab your child drags a lens over a leaf to find veins, edge hairs and an aphid, adjusts it until the view is sharp, chooses looking words for a shell, compares two similar leaves, sorts questions onto tools and picks the safe way to use a lens.

practice.prompt: A hand lens shows tiny hairs on a leaf. Were the hairs there before you looked?
choices: Yes, they were too small to see
Only while the lens is there
practice.hint: Does a lens change the leaf, or only how it looks to your eyes?
practice.explain: The hairs were always there. The lens only makes them look bigger so you can see them.

practice.prompt: Which words tell a friend most about a shell?
practice.hint: Pick words about colour, shape or how it feels.
practice.explain: Brown is a colour and bumpy is a texture. Nice and good say what you think, not what you see.

practice.prompt: With a lens you count {a} spots on one ladybird and {b} spots on another. How many spots altogether?
practice.hint: Count on from the first ladybird's spots.
practice.explain: {a} spots and {b} spots make {=a+b} spots altogether.

practice.prompt: You want to know how long a worm is. Which tool do you use?
practice.hint: This 'how long' is about length, not time.
practice.explain: A ruler measures length. A lens shows small details and a timer measures time.

practice.prompt: Leaf 1 has {a} veins on one side. Leaf 2 has {b} veins on one side. How many more does leaf 1 have?
practice.hint: Find the difference: count on from the smaller number to the bigger one.
practice.explain: {a} take away {b} is {=a-b}, so leaf 1 has {=a-b} more veins.

pool.prompt: The view through the lens is blurry. What should you do?
choices: Move the lens until it looks sharp
Press the lens flat on the leaf
pool.hint: Try a little closer, then a little farther.
pool.explain: A view is sharp only at the right distance. Move the lens a bit until the details are clear.

pool.prompt: Can you look at the Sun through a hand lens?
pool.hint: Think about keeping your eyes safe.
pool.explain: Never look at the Sun, with or without a lens. It can hurt your eyes. A lens in sunshine can also start a fire.

pool.prompt: Two leaves look the same from far away. How do you check?
choices: Look closely at both, side by side
pool.explain: Look at both with a lens, side by side. Then you can say what is the same and what is different.

pool.hint: Texture is how something feels or looks like it feels.
pool.explain: Rough is a texture. Red is a colour and round is a shape.

pool.prompt: You want to see how long an ice cube takes to melt. Which tool do you use?
pool.explain: A timer measures time. A ruler measures length and a lens shows small details.

pool.prompt: Under the lens you count {a} ants on a stone. Then {b} walk away. How many are left?
pool.hint: Take away the ants that walked off.
pool.explain: {a} take away {b} leaves {=a-b} ants on the stone.

pool.prompt: A lens makes a seed look {z} times as long. The seed is {s} mm long. How long does it look?
pool.explain: {z} lots of {s} mm is {=s*z} mm. The seed itself is still {s} mm long.

pool.prompt: Mia says the lens made the ant bigger. What is right?
pool.hint: Take the lens away. What size is the ant?
pool.explain: A lens changes how the ant looks to you, not the ant itself. Without the lens it is the same small ant.

pool.prompt: Which is the best way to describe a feather?
pool.hint: Use colour, texture and size words.
pool.explain: Grey is a colour, soft is a texture and long is a size. Those words tell someone what you saw.
